newsitem.title: USA: American Express has better-than-expected earnings.
newsitem.headline: American Express has better-than-expected earnings.

text.p: American Express Co. on Monday reported seecond-quarter profits that came in a shade above forecasts on Wall Street.

The financial services giant said net profit rose to $520 million, or $1.08 a share, for the quarter, from $452 million, or 93 cents a share, a year earlier. Wall Street analysts had forecast earnings of $1.06 a share for the latest quarter, according to First Call, which tracks estimates.
Sales rose 8 percent to $4.42 billion from $4.08 billion.

"These results were in line with American Express' long-term targets of 12 percent to 15 percent earnings-per-share growth, with at least 8 percent coming from higher revenues," the company said in a statement.

The company, based in New York, said its Travel Related Services unit, the largest of its three divisions in terms of income, had earnings of $355 million for the quarter, compared with $322 million a year ago.
Travel services sales grew 7 percent on growth worldwide and growth in card member loans outstanding, it said.
American Express is a global travel, financial and network services provider.
